question: Article 13 of the Cotonou Agreement deals with the issue of migration, particularly the repatriation of migrants to their home countries, but it has been described as ‘largely ineffective’12. The Samoa agreement deals with migration particularly in Articles 70 to 75 (title VI, part II), in addition to Annex 1, which relates to returns and readmissions.3 1.

‘In 2022, 73,600 non-EU citizens were returned to a non-EU country. This corresponds to 17% of all return decisions issued during the year, decreasing from 18% in 2021.’4The rates of return were particularly low for some countries signatory to the Cotonou Agreement, such as Côte d'Ivoire (2.7%) and Guinea (4.3%). In light of these figures, what is the Commission’s assessment of the effectiveness of the Cotonou agreement, particularly Article 13?
How will the Commission ensure the Samoa agreement can be used to address migration successfully (see the above quotes)?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.5.2024) The EU Pact for Migration and Asylum1 works towards a comprehensive and balanced European approach aimed at building a system that manages and normalises migration in the long term. Return and readmission are essential elements of this approach and of a credible migration policy.

Therefore, fostering returns of irregular migrants is a priority on which the Commission is intensifying engagement with third countries. Article 13 of the Cotonou agreement2 provided for dialogue and cooperation on legal and irregular migration, including return and readmission, but did not set concrete rules and procedures on enforcement.

The new Partnership Agreement between the EU and its Member States, and the Members of the Organisation of the African, Caribbean and Pacific States (Samoa agreement3) includes a title on migration and mobility. All Parties agreed on the need to enhance cooperation on all facets of migration through a balanced and comprehensive approach.

Compared to its precursor, the new agreement deepens cooperation on return and readmission. It contains a binding legal obligation for all signatories to readmit irregular migrants, without conditionality and without further formalities other than the verification of nationality. The commitments will be monitored through the regular partnership dialogue.

The new agreement also sets out that if a Party considers that another Party has failed to respect the time limit of 30 days4, it shall notify the other Party. If that other Party continues to breach those obligations, the notifying Party may take proportionate measures 30 days after the notification.
Lastly, a legally binding Annex details the readmission process, including by clarifying means to ascertain verification of nationality.
